comparator.academicYear: Current published UvA bachelor curriculum, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official programme is 180 EC over three years. Year 1 is a fixed 60-EC foundation in human geography, spatial planning, urban dynamics, academic skills, GIS, quantitative methods and a regional project. For year 2, the generic target requires one of three 18-EC specialisations; Planning is selected by the neutral official-order tie-break, with coherent planning electives instantiated from the official restricted-choice lists. Year 2 also includes 24 EC of methods and field projects. Year 3 contains a 12-EC thematic elective, 6 EC of thesis methods, 30 EC genuine free choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. The English and bilingual routes have the same curriculum.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target names no specialisation. The official curriculum lists Planning, Human Geography, and Global Urbanism and Transnational Planning as equally substantial 18-EC year-2 specialisations and does not identify one as general. Planning appears first, so it is selected neutrally and independently of UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest programme integrates the target’s social-spatial, environmental and mixed-method core. The Human Geography and Global Urbanism directions are separately evidenced by official specialisations and produce materially different governance/inequality and transnational-place curricula. All three are mechanically feasible and pairwise differ by at least nine courses, so production stops at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: UvA provides a continuous disciplinary sequence in human geography and spatial planning, including dedicated GIS, field projects, planning theory, a named specialisation and a bachelor thesis. UCR can combine strong sociology, politics, economics, sustainability, environmental science, data and research courses, but the fixed Fall 2026 catalogue does not offer the same full geography-and-planning sequence. The UCR alternatives therefore cover related subjects and methods without claiming professional planning equivalence.
